Do not trust these cowboys.

At first they appear very friendly and helpful, but my experience changed very quickly.

I purchased a Vehicle from them and, after only around two months, it developed an emissions-related issue. I was under the impression that the problem had been dealt with under the warranty.

I have since discovered that work had been carried out on the vehicle which involved an illegal modification to the emissions system and breaches emissions laws. The vehicle was subsequently found to have been tampered with, leaving me with a vehicle that was not in a road-legal condition.

What makes this particularly concerning is that I trusted the vehicle had been properly repaired when I was told the issue had been dealt with.

I am now having to deal with the finance company and an independent inspection to establish exactly what happened and who was responsible.

My advice to anyone considering buying a vehicle from this company is do your own checks and get an independent inspection before buying. My experience has been extremely disappointing and has caused a lot of unnecessary stress and expense.

This business is a potential threat to life, and ought not to be supported.  The way that I was treated is also the way that your loved ones might be treated.  Details below.

At 9.25am on 17 August 2026, I was cycling west from Didcot towards Harwell.  A Millbrook Services van was following me.  An overtake would have been unsafe due to a pedestrian crossing and also oncoming traffic, so I rode in centre of the lane (see Highway Code rule 72(1)).  As soon as it was safe to overtake, I dropped in to allow the driver to do so (see rule 72(2)).  The driver then had a huge width of road available for a safe overtake (see rule 163), but instead chose to pass as close to me as possible, while accelerating.  This can only be explained as deliberate attempt to "punish" me for having added a few seconds to his journey by riding in accordance with the Highway Code rather than allowing him to squeeze through dangerously when there was oncoming traffic.  He passed me so close as to cause a significant risk of collision, which could have caused me serious injury or worse.  If I had been using my camera at the time, then he would now be looking at at least six penalty points on his licence if not more.

one_star_reviews.text:
Extremely disappointing and, based on my experience, a deeply upsetting lack of empathy.

I had been a patient at this clinic since 2024 and had been treated by Dr Sandeep. During that time, I had always attended my appointments and had never previously missed one. I have a longstanding issue that has required ongoing treatment, which is why I continued attending the clinic over the past two years.

After returning to university and moving across London, my circumstances changed significantly. I was no longer based in Camberley and could only return during university holidays. I was genuinely struggling to manage my schedule, and because my university commitments and availability were unpredictable, I unfortunately and unintentionally missed two appointments.

I completely understand that missed appointments affect a small clinic and that there are policies surrounding non-attendance. I accept responsibility for missing those appointments. What I found extremely upsetting, however, was that when I contacted the clinic, apologised and explained my circumstances, I felt that there was absolutely no consideration given to my previous two years as a patient or to the circumstances behind the missed appointments.

Instead, I was told that I had been discharged from the clinic and that any future appointments I attempted to book would automatically be rejected.

What disappointed me most was not simply the decision itself, but the way it was communicated. The response ended with: “I hope you find an appointment elsewhere.”

After being a patient there since 2024, having consistently attended appointments previously, and having a longstanding issue that required ongoing treatment, I found that response incredibly cold, dismissive and insensitive.

I was not asking the clinic to ignore its policy. I was asking for some understanding and consideration of the circumstances. There is a significant difference between enforcing a non-attendance policy and making a longstanding patient feel that they are simply no longer welcome.

I understand that missed appointments can cost a small clinic money. I also understand that clinics need boundaries and policies. But in my opinion, policies can be enforced while still treating people with basic understanding, dignity, respect and compassion.

Unfortunately, that was not my experience.

I left this interaction feeling extremely disappointed and dismissed, particularly because of the length of time I had been a patient and the fact that I had previously attended consistently.

For a healthcare clinic, I believe empathy and compassion should matter just as much as policies. This experience has left a very negative impression on me, and I would not have expected to be treated this way after being a longstanding patient.

A very upsetting experience, and one that I genuinely wish had been handled with more understanding and humanity.

I had two stints in this facility.
My experience at Recovery Lighthouse in Worthing was extremely concerning and left me feeling unsafe. Men were allowed into my room while staff were asleep overnight and not watching the cameras, which we're supposed to protect me in an extreme vulnerable state.
Obviously completely unacceptable and made me question the level of supervision and safeguarding in place.

I also witnessed people openly taking drugs on the premises. I was further concerned by blind spots in the CCTV coverage, which raised questions for me about how effectively residents could be monitored and protected.

A recovery facility should provide a safe, secure and supportive environment for people who may be particularly vulnerable. Based on my personal experience, I did not feel that these basic expectations were being met.

I hope management takes these concerns seriously, reviews staff supervision and safeguarding procedures, and ensures that residents are properly protected in the future.

one_star_reviews.text:
I unfortunately had a really poor experience with this garage.
I had my car serviced at the end of July as I was travelling to Europe the following week and wanted to make sure it was safe and fully functioning. The service highlighted that my front suspension arms needed replacing, which we booked in that week.
Unfortunately, after this work, two issues arose.

The first, and most serious, was a complete loss of braking whilst driving through Germany, caused by a leak in the rear-left brake cylinder. Thankfully, this happened whilst driving through a quiet village rather than on the Autobahn or mountain roads I had been driving on earlier, as this could have been extremely dangerous.
What concerns me most is that the service report had marked all areas relating to the rear brakes as green, including visual checks of the rear brakes, brake calipers for leaks and security, and brake pipes and hoses. The garage uses a red, amber and green system and provides a full printout of these checks. The German mechanic described the failure as significant and was surprised it had not been picked up during a service.

When I raised this with the garage, they offered no solution and stated that my service did not include a proper inspection of the rear brakes because it was a “small service”. This was not explained to us when we booked the service, we were simply quoted a price. I feel customers should be clearly told what is and isn’t included before booking, and that as standard breaks should always be thoroughly checked no matter the service. Furthermore, if the brakes are only being externally checked, I don’t believe they should be marked green, as this gives the impression that they have been assessed as safe when there may be underlying issues.
The second issue relates to the handbrake. After the suspension-arm work, the handbrake warning light came on and would not switch off. I contacted the garage and agreed to bring it back when I returned to the UK.

When my brakes failed in Germany, the mechanic also inspected the handbrake and found that the cable on one side had seized. He released it temporarily and advised me to have it replaced when I returned to the UK. After leaving the garage, I noticed that the handbrake warning light had gone off.
When I returned, I asked the original garage to inspect the handbrake and replace the faulty cable at no cost, as the issue had only arisen following their work. They refused any responsibility, stating that the suspension arms were at the front of the vehicle and therefore unrelated to the handbrake. While I understand they are separate components, the handbrake had been functioning before the work and the issue arose immediately afterwards. I felt it was reasonable to expect them to investigate this rather than simply dismissing responsibility.

Overall, I am very disappointed. I was initially impressed by the garage and thought their red, amber and green system was transparent and easy to understand. However, after these experiences and the response I received, it now feels more like a tick-box exercise. Most importantly, I no longer feel confident that I can trust the garage to understand the responsibility they have, alongside me as the driver, to ensure a car is safe to drive

Unfortunately, I had an extremely disappointing experience with this shop.

I placed an order for a custom-made dress for a wedding and was very clear about exactly what I wanted. I showed the lady a reference picture of the dress, took additional photos, and explained specifically how I wanted it to look. I also stressed how important this dress was to me and asked her to keep me updated on the progress so that any issues could be addressed before the dress was completed. She agreed to take on the job and quoted me £350.

Unfortunately, I received no progress updates at all. The next time I saw the dress was when it was delivered, and I was genuinely shocked by what I received. It looked nothing like what we had agreed.

The dress was supposed to have significant gathering along the sides and gathering at the back, as clearly shown in the reference picture and discussed beforehand. Instead, it arrived with just three pleats on the side and no gathering at the back.

What shocked me even more was that the dress did not even have a lining. A custom-made dress costing £350 with no lining whatsoever was extremely disappointing and, in my opinion, completely unacceptable for the price being charged.

I had paid a £200 deposit, with the remaining £150 due upon delivery. Had the dress been made as agreed and to the standard I was expecting, I would have had absolutely no problem paying the full £350. My issue was never the price. My issue was the quality of what I actually received for that price.

I have included a picture of the dress I asked for alongside a picture of the dress that was actually made. I think the pictures speak for themselves, so you can judge the difference for yourselves.

I could not accept or take the dress home. I tried to resolve the situation amicably, but unfortunately I found the response extremely rude. Despite the dress not being made according to what we had agreed, she refused to refund my £200 deposit.

I will be fair and say that the shop does have some lovely items. However, based on my experience, I would personally be very cautious about ordering a custom-made dress from here. Dresses do not always turn out perfectly and mistakes can happen. For me, the biggest issue was how the situation was handled afterwards. When a customer has clearly explained what they want, provided pictures and paid a substantial deposit, I would expect the business to take some responsibility when the finished product is significantly different from what was agreed.

I was left without the dress I had ordered, £200 out of pocket, and with only two days to find another dress for the wedding.

A horrible, stressful and deeply disappointing experience.

1-Star Review – Extremely Disappointing Experience

I would strongly advise people to be very careful when dealing with Specialist Recruitment Solutions Limited (SRS).

I was repeatedly contacted by an employee named Jimmy regarding recruitment opportunities. I was sent to DPD on multiple occasions and was told there was work available, but when I arrived, there was apparently no requirement. Despite this, Jimmy continued contacting me and asking me to attend again.

On more than one occasion, I made the journey based on what I had been told, only for the shift to be cancelled or for nothing to happen. There was no proper onboarding, no enrolment and no actual start of work. This has resulted in a significant waste of my time, travel and effort.

What made the situation even worse was the communication afterwards. When I tried calling Jimmy to get an explanation or clarification, my calls were repeatedly avoided/not answered.

If you are recruiting people for work, you should have the basic courtesy and professionalism to make sure the work actually exists before repeatedly sending candidates to a workplace. People have jobs, commitments, travel costs and responsibilities.

My personal experience with SRS has been extremely poor. I found the entire process misleading, frustrating and completely unprofessional. I would not recommend this recruitment company based on my experience.

one_star_reviews.text:
I am autistic, and my experience of the National Adult ADHD and Autism Psychology Service (NAAAPS) at the Maudsley Hospital was, on balance, a rather negative one that adversely affected my mental health. I would have posted this sooner, but personal circumstances and necessary prioritisation prevented me.

My initial contact with the senior clinical psychologist was by email. I felt that information I shared in one of my replies was dismissed.

In January 2024, before my face-to-face assessment, she telephoned me to learn more about my circumstances. One of her questions was "Are you violent?" I appreciate that screening for violence is a routine part of clinical assessment. However, as an autistic person with a history of trauma and longstanding social anxiety, I found the question, as it was put, distressing. A gentler approach, such as a brief explanation of why the question is asked, would have been more consistent with trauma-informed practice.

The service also told me how long the online pre-assessment questionnaire would take and I was happy to complete a questionnaire, but it took me considerably longer to complete the questionnaire. I raised this with her on two separate occasions, and particularly on the first occasion I found her response a negative experience.

I also found the physical environment difficult. At my February 2024 assessment there was no heating in the consulting room, and I needed to put my insulated jacket back on to keep warm. At my first psychology session in spring 2025, the room was dim because the lighting was inoperable. For autistic patients, the sensory environment matters.

After my assessment, I was sent a draft psychology assessment report and invited to suggest amendments. I did so, and she told me she would use my amended draft. She did not fully do this.

At the beginning of the first psychology session in the spring 2025 I told the psychologist I needed to postpone further psychology sessions, as I was concerned about overcommitting and becoming overwhelmed. Autistic people are at markedly higher risk of overwhelm, and I had hoped a trained senior clinical psychologist in a specialist autism service would respond with empathy and understanding. Instead, I experienced her response as dismissive. I felt I was misrepresented on two occasions, and I felt that guilt was being placed on me. Almost three years passed between my GP's referral to NAAAPS and my first psychology session with the clinical psychologist. In that time, my daily schedule changed, and had the sessions started sooner, I would not have needed to postpone the further sessions.

When I was attending the NAAAPS, I also noticed that she was offering private psychological support through a website on which she describes herself as warm and compassionate. That did not reflect my experience across one telephone call, a face-to-face assessment and a face-to-face psychology session, during which I felt uncomfortable.

In summer 2025, after careful consideration, I informed her that I was declining the remaining psychology sessions scheduled to begin that September, as it was not the right fit for me at that time. I am exploring art therapy and autism-focused resources instead.

On the plus side, the psychology assessment report was thorough and included some positive observations about me. I also appreciated that NAAAPS is a gender-inclusive service.

I share this in the hope that the service will reflect on how communication style, sensory environment, and trauma-informed practice shape the experience of autistic patients.

Shocking Lack of Communication and Careless Mistakes

Placed an order for Saxon School uniform on July 31st. Their website promises a 7–10 working day turnaround and promises to notify customers if there are any delays.

​Over three weeks passed with zero communication. I even went to the Shepperton store in person hoping it was ready, only to leave empty-handed. I finally had to chase them up myself on August 22nd. Magically, after emailing back today 24/08/26 with excuses about sourcing a small cardigan size, they emailed later that same day claiming it was ready for collection.

​The chaos didn't end there. When I picked up the order and got home, a polo shirt was completely missing from the bag. I had to make yet another trip back to the store to report it. Their response? Another apology, repeating the same excuse about the cardigan, and admitting they just forgot to pack the polo shirt.

​With school starting imminently, sitting on an order for nearly a month, making customers chase updates, and completely failing basic order packing is unacceptable. A school uniform supplier should know how to handle peak season. Unreliable, disorganized, and frustrating service.

We ultimately decided to go with another company and, so far, the experience has been much more positive. Thankfully, we hadn’t invested too much time or money into the process before making that decision.

I booked a lash lift and brow lamination at Brow Lodge. The treatment itself took place in a very pleasant atmosphere, but unfortunately, the final result was far from what I had expected. I’m attaching a photo so that everyone can decide for themselves whether this is the right place for them, as I personally was very disappointed. I also have a few concerns about the way the treatment was carried out.

Once I had to keep my eyes closed for the duration of the treatment, I was asked to choose a brow tint colour based solely on the name of the shade. I asked the beautician to choose a colour that would match my hair, but unfortunately, my eyebrows ended up being significantly darker than I had expected.

Despite having a patch test approximately a week before the treatment, towards the end of the lash lift my eyes started burning and watering very badly. I experienced a strong, burning sensation on my eyelids. Once the product was removed, the burning subsided, but I left the salon with blurred vision. I couldn’t properly see what my lashes looked like, but I felt that I had been looked after and left in a positive mood.

However, once I got home, I noticed that on one eye my lashes were curling towards my eyelid, with some of the lashes crossing over each other and forming sharp kinks.

Unfortunately, all of this happened just before I was due to go on holiday, so my only option now is to nourish my damaged, stiff lashes with castor oil and wear sunglasses.

I would not recommend having this treatment at Brow Lodge.

Latest update — evidence and accountability

This review has received 2,063 views.

I accept professional boundaries. My first key worker, Margarida, deserves recognition. After more than ten years fighting addiction, my son gave me the strongest reason to change, but recovery does not happen overnight. Margarida gave me another push, belief and strength. She made me feel listened to, respected and seen as a person, not an addiction or case file. When things were bad, I trusted her; when good, I looked forward to telling her.

She once said she was only doing her job and I was doing the hard work. She was right, but what feels small to a worker can be monumental to the person receiving it.

In many ways, Margarida represented the very meaning of Change, Grow, Live. She helped somebody change, encouraged him to grow, and contributed to him wanting to properly live again. I often describe exceptional NHS doctors and nurses as true angels. I put Margarida in that same category: a quiet, compassionate professional angel whose impact may be greater than she realises.

I also recognise Anandhu, who has dealt with me decently through a hard period, and Richard more cautiously; fairness means acknowledging when he treated me decently.

Stage 3 found the restriction decision by Dr Kostas Agath and Robert Cathrew flawed, presumptive and insufficiently documented, with no clear rationale. My account was not properly considered and the other-service information was sparse, unsubstantiated and later incorrect.

Dr Kostas recorded clinical-sounding judgments despite saying he was not assessing me. He interpreted what I intended as a sincere, emotional message of thanks and apology in a way I believe distorted its meaning. I am strongly expressive in how I speak and write; emotion is not itself evidence of pathology, manipulation or risk. From a Consultant Psychiatrist I expected curiosity, context and care. Stage 3 found his language negative, subjective and not trauma-informed.

Robert described me as “aggressive” and “combative”, which I still do not believe was evidenced. Stage 3 recommended reflective supervision for him on evidence-based decisions and checking assumptions.

Matthew Worboys repeated subjective wording at Stage 1, further inflaming my distress. An internal note records Matthew suggesting Sundeep be emailed and Dr Kostas copied “re NK”, adding Kostas would “offer guidance re NK”. As Kostas’s conduct formed part of my complaint, this raises an unresolved independence question. It does not prove collusion, but deserves an answer.

My SAR recorded a Stage 2 discussion involving Sundeep Thandi and Dr Kostas referring to “Fixation on a Single Issue”, “His attachment to the issue / Best communication style” and my complaint being “psychologically unresolved”. Sundeep later assured me Kostas had not been involved in reviewing, advising on or influencing decisions after I raised concerns. I cannot reconcile that with the records.

Nichola Armitage identified important failings, and I credit her. But key contradictions remained unresolved. I hoped an Operational Director would sift the record, test contradictions and press for answers. Stage 3 offered writing; I chose it, yet CGL later refused further substantive written complaint responses and moved matters towards a meeting. My “high volume of emails” contained evidence because answers remained elusive.

Stage 3 recommended a restriction review under Minesh Patel involving Donna Martin, and reflective supervision for Dr Kostas, Robert and Matthew.

I am not asking for dismissal. But “learning” cannot become the automatic answer to serious professional failures. Where evidence justifies it, there should be proportionate disciplinary accountability, supervision and retraining.

Margarida showed me what Change, Grow, Live can genuinely mean. If CGL corrects the record, applies proportionate accountability and learns from what happened, I will say so publicly.

Unfortunately, I am one of the few who had a negative experience with this Shariah Council. It took me a year to get the divorce because the ex husband was withholding divorce and not cooperating which prolonged the process despite the fact we were seperated.  In my experience, greater training and awareness around domestic abuse is needed. Someone leaving an abusive marriage should not be expected to mediate with their spouse, particularly where there are safety concerns. I approached the council seeking an Islamic dissolution after leaving my marriage due to domestic abuse. I found parts of the process unnecessarily prolonged and emotionally difficult, more so being expected to engage in mediation/reconciliation despite the circumstances I had disclosed.
I believe cases involving domestic abuse should be approached differently from ordinary marital disputes, with greater consideration given to safeguarding and the impact that continued engagement with an abusive spouse can have on the person seeking a dissolution. I also felt that the council's approach to remaining neutral did not always result in a fair process. Neutrality in cases involving domestic abuse needs to take account of the circumstances and power dynamics involved, rather than treating both parties as though they are simply two spouses in an ordinary marital dispute. I really hope this is taken on board.

Premium price, disposable design, dreadful after-sales support

I would strongly advise against buying this kettle.

I bought a Bosch Sky TWK7203GB expecting the usual Bosch quality and longevity. The kettle itself is still working perfectly. What has failed is a tiny plastic latch that holds the lid closed.

That single piece of plastic has effectively written off the entire appliance.

I contacted Bosch assuming this would be a straightforward repair: sell me the latch, sell me a replacement lid, or offer some sensible repair option.

Bosch has confirmed in writing that neither the latch nor the complete lid is available as a spare part.

Their solution is for me to pay to send the whole kettle to a workshop, where they will inspect an already obvious mechanical fault and only then tell me how much they want to charge to repair it.

I repeatedly asked Bosch to consider a goodwill solution. They refused, simply because the two-year warranty had expired.

That is an appalling approach to product longevity.

This is not a heating element failing after years of heavy use. It is not an electrical fault. It is a small plastic catch on an otherwise fully functioning appliance, and Bosch has apparently designed the product so that this essential component cannot simply be replaced.

The result is that a perfectly usable electrical appliance may now end up in the bin because of a tiny piece of plastic.

That makes Bosch/BSH's public messaging about sustainability, durability and repairability look extremely hollow.

The most frustrating part is that I deliberately paid more for Bosch because I believed I was buying a better-made product from a company that would support it properly. Instead, I have ended up with what is effectively a disposable kettle once one minor non-serviceable component fails.

Bosch customer service was also repeatedly evasive. It took several emails just to obtain a clear answer about whether the lid was available, and repeated requests for goodwill consideration and escalation were met largely with variations of “the warranty has expired”.

For anyone considering this model, I would think very carefully before paying a premium for it. The kettle may look and feel well made, but if the lid latch breaks, Bosch cannot sell you the part you need to put it right.

A premium appliance should not become e-waste because of a tiny plastic clip.

Based on both the product design and Bosch's response afterwards, I would not buy this kettle again and I would be very reluctant to buy another Bosch small appliance.

My experience with Caroline Lister was extremely disappointing.

During my family court proceedings, I became concerned about the way matters were being presented to the court and CAFCASS. I felt that CAFCASS recommendations and wording were not always being accurately represented, and I experienced attempts to have me undergo a psychiatric assessment which I strongly disputed.

There were also occasions where wording appeared in proposed orders that I did not believe had actually been ordered by the court. On one occasion, I had to ask the judge to rewrite an order before it could be sealed. On another occasion, an order was subsequently rescinded after I disputed the suggestion that I had agreed to it.

For me, the cumulative effect of these issues was extremely distressing and, in my view, had a detrimental impact on my child.

Ultimately, I successfully obtained a barring order and Caroline Lister was no longer involved in the case. Since then, the other parent and I have been able to communicate and co parent peacefully, spend family time together, and most importantly, our child is happy again.

I cannot help but wonder whether, had my case been handled differently from the beginning, we could have reached this point much earlier.

Based entirely on my own experience, I would not recommend Caroline Lister. My experience was that the damage caused by the way the case was handled was far greater than any benefit I felt her involvement provided.

This review reflects my personal experience and my understanding of what occurred during my case.

I had (online) couples therapy at the Tavistock in 2021, the model used was neither attachment centred or trauma informed. My experience was an approach that uncovered conflict but did not have a process that helped move to an understanding of self or the other. Nor was a safe foundation built at the start, it took until the final session (half way) for the therapist to ask what brought us together.

It might be an approach that works for securely attached couples. But if you had a childhood where parents were emotionally distant, or displayed excessive anger etc... this is not a therapeutic model I'd recommend.

As an organisation that was formative in attachment theory, I hope that there is consideration about using a model that has grown from this.

If you are looking for therapy, look at the work of Dr Sue Johnson.

I hope a new business takes over there and welcomes people to their classes and has consistent rules for everyone.

one_star_reviews.text:
Sadly, our experience fell considerably short of what we expected from private maternity care.
During our complex twin pregnancy, which tragically ended with the loss of both our babies in the second trimester, we often felt that information and guidance during scans were kept to a minimum. Given the complexity of the pregnancy, we had expected clearer explanations, more proactive guidance and greater specialist input.
We were also disappointed by the lack of clarity around the pregnancy package and additional costs. Despite 24/7 personal mobile contact being presented as part of the package, our calls and messages during this incredibly difficult period were later catalogued, alongside a suggestion that charging for them individually would result in a considerably higher amount.
Throughout such a vulnerable experience, we had hoped for greater transparency, sensitivity and a genuinely patient-centred approach. Based on our experience, we would not choose this practice again, particularly for a complex or twin pregnancy.

The experience here was extremely disappointing. The manager and staff were very rude and unpleasant.

They have a section selling second-hand clothing, but the prices are extremely high — in some cases almost the same as buying the item new. I was interested in a pair of trousers that had some damage, although they were otherwise in reasonable condition, so I politely asked whether they could lower the price given the damage. Instead of discussing it with me, the staff member was extremely rude and dismissive and refused to even have a proper conversation about it.

If a business is going to promote sustainability and sell second-hand clothing, I would expect the prices and customer service to reflect that ethos. Charging almost-new prices for damaged second-hand items and then treating customers poorly when they reasonably question the price feels very contradictory to the sustainability message.

The manager was terrible, and the staff were equally unpleasant. Unfortunately, I would not recommend this place.

one_star_reviews.text: I swear to deal with customer services at this clinic is actually detrimental to mental health. The cost at the clinic is the most expensive in London but it doesn’t reflect on the end product. I was referred by a friend I’m actually embarrassed to tell her how bad it is!

I warn parents against using this place all the time and I have told my child's school that they should warn parents away from here too.

The practice manager told me quite openly that The Giaroli Centre were struggling due to the fast pace of their company's expansion and I'm afraid it shows. The lack of personal attention and care here is astounding and communication is non-existent between the doctors, their admin teams and patients. As a patient, you truly are a number in a system - the overall feeling we were left with was that they don't care about your child, but they really do care about payments.

The 1st doctor that we saw - who I won't name - was thoroughly disorganised in our meetings with them and we were left with absolutely no faith at all in their ability. Our son's initial report was clearly a cut and paste template with glaring inaccuracies, including the wrong names for his parents, his age and year at school and many, many more. He was also misdiagnosed initially by this first doctor; we were told he needed an additional assessment for a different condition but subsequently, 2 other doctors at the Giaroli Centre said he did have the condition he was initially assessed for. No explanation was given as to why he was misdiagnosed.

To give you an idea of how difficult it is to deal with this company, I had to lodge a formal complaint (which I didn't want to do!) just in order to get someone to call me back to arrange additional assessments. In the end, I used a practitioner outside the Giaroli for one of the assessments because the Giaroli Centre just wouldn't respond.

Of the 3 doctors we saw at the Giaroli, 1 was excellent and 2 were very much below our expectations, actually leaving my son feeling very uncertain after his meetings with them. For example, 1 of the doctors didn't even introduce themselves to me or my 7 year old son as we entered the room, and I was then immediately told to leave. My son - who is usually extremely confident and gregarious - was terrified at the thought of being left in a closed room with an adult they'd never met before, without any warning. Not quite the bedside manner you'd hope for from professionals who work with young children on a daily basis!

Another reviewer has mentioned that they were charged an additional £300 for a "follow-up consultation" without being told - the same thing happened to us where a £300 payment was put onto my card without notification, for a final consultation which never happened. It is clearly illegal to hold card details and then to take unauthorised payments without clear and explicit consent.

I cannot stress enough how I would avoid this company at all costs.

Very disappointed with how this practice handled a simple prescription reissue. My son had a valid prescription that expired while we were abroad — through no fault of ours, we simply couldn’t get to a pharmacy in time. When I asked to have it reissued, I was told I’d need to pay full consultation price again, as if it were a brand new appointment.

The staff member I spoke to even admitted this is a common complaint from other patients, yet the practice still refuses to offer any flexibility. Prescription fees here are unreasonably high to begin with, and charging full price again just to reissue something already approved feels excessive and more about revenue than patient care.

Otherwise the medical care here has been fine, but this billing practice around reissuance is disgraceful and needs to change.

Unfortunately, we had an extremely disappointing experience at the entrance to Maddox Club.

My friend and I were on the guest list and were both appropriately dressed in blazer dresses and heels. Two female members of staff at the door, presumably hostesses, repeatedly and very obviously looked us up and down from head to toe with unpleasant, judgmental expressions. I work in the fashion industry and fully understand that high-end venues have certain dress codes and door policies, but there was absolutely nothing inappropriate about our appearance or the way we were dressed.
Eventually, they told us that we could enter, but their attitude had already made us feel so uncomfortable that I directly told them that the way they were treating us was not appropriate. One of them stepped towards me and continued with the same arrogant attitude, implying that this was simply part of her job. Making guests feel uncomfortable and unwelcome should never be part of anyone’s job in hospitality.
What shocked me even more was what happened when I asked for their names because I intended to make a complaint. They both gave me the same name and laughed. In my opinion, this was extremely unprofessional and immature behaviour.
Despite being allowed entry, we chose to leave without even entering the club.
I completely respect a venue’s right to maintain its standards and door policy. What I do not respect is staff making guests feel judged, mocked or unwelcome. There is a difference between being selective and simply being rude.
For a venue that positions itself at this level, I would expect considerably more professionalism and basic respect from the people representing it at the door.

Booked in with this Chiropractic clinic due to my insurance approving 5 sessions, At first not really impressed 1 consultation is used up a session, best practice is to merge the consultation along with the first session or provide a free consultation so wasnt pleased with that.

In regards to my first session I had with Alex was very unwelcoming and felt rushed with the consultation. In regards to booking my remaining sessions and treatment plan appointments are not available with the main qualified Chiropractor Paula who is authorised to do the treatment by BUPA and accredited, I was told Paula isnt available and I had a range of 4 practitioners, Alex, Paula, Chris and Sam. Not only was timing and availability very scarce around my working life I was seen by various people and not the same person. I was booked in with Alex first only to be told hes going on holiday for a few weeks.

Each and every session lasted around 5 to 10 mins, felt very rushed with around 2 adjustments and each practitioner didnt have a clue about my conditions and I had to explain every time including one making a very unpleasing comment about my back acne which doesnt help my confidence for a long term condition im managing. Have seen no effects and not amused at all. Reported to Bupa who have confirmed this is fraud to Bupa and that I shouldnt have been seen by multiple practitioners and it should have only been Paula and the sessions shouldnt have lasted that long as Bupa even agreed we dont even know if Chris, Sam and Alex are properly qualified and they are now investigating this and opened an investigation as of today on the clinic.

On my last session I wasnt notified that my insurance sessions are over and was demanded payment which put me under pressure which I refused to pay and had to get my insurance to provide an emergency intervention which I was not amused about. This communication should have been informed to me.

I am now having to rebook with another clinic and start my sessions all over again which is a massive inconvenience and I wouldnt recommend this practice at all especially if handling with Insurance too. Measly 5 minute sessions and no results.

VWFS and CarMoney are now refusing to refund my £6,000 deposit and passing the blame back and forth on who will be refunding me even though the adjudication was accepted on 5th August 2026, they had originally accepted rejection of my vehicle on 17th July 2026.

My vehicle rejection dispute has been ongoing since March 2026 where I had to made hundreds of phone calls and emails plus I was made to pay £2,340 for a vehicle inspection report because my complaint was declined after 7 weeks and 2 days with no contact what so ever.

I also submitted a complaint on 12 August 2026 and have had no response from CarMoney what so ever.

We are now at 1st September 2026 without receiving a single penny.

I have had to involve solicitors with a letter of claim being submitted to VWFS, the deadline to put the resolution in place set by the FOS is 3rd September and if this is not completed they are in breach of a legally binding decision.

I would strongly suggest avoiding both CarMoney and Volkswagen Financial Services for any finance related matters.

I have attached screenshots of emails and text messages as proof of the above.

I have been waiting 6 months and was made to keep paying my monthly instalments which have finally been stopped today.

CarMoney and VWFS, you have until 3rd September to refund my deposit, I do not care who it is, take ownership and get it done.

Unfortunately, this was the worst Chaiwala experience we’ve had.

* EDIT/UPDATE:

Neil Douglas has now found the time to publish a lengthy and sarcastic response to this review. The pigeon problem itself remains unresolved.

For clarity, we are now at approximately eight weeks and 22 emails concerning pigeons fouling residents’ patios.

The selectively quoted message in Neil Douglas’s response was my second email, sent near the beginning of this process, when I believed the matter was being handled promptly. Eight weeks of correspondence and continued inaction have obviously changed that assessment. Presenting an early expression of thanks without that context is misleading.

Their response also characterises pigeon fouling affecting residents’ homes as merely an “inconvenience” affecting a “small number of properties,” before accusing me of giving the managing agent a “public kicking.” I think that tone speaks for itself.

Whether final authority rests with Neil Douglas or the resident management company is immaterial to my experience as a customer: Neil Douglas is the appointed managing agent, the issue was reported to them, and after eight weeks and 22 emails it remains unresolved.

The fact that a detailed public rebuttal could be produced more quickly than an effective resolution rather neatly proves the original point of this review. Perhaps just do better!

Original review:
Nearly seven weeks and 10 emails to deal with a basic pest control issue, and it still isn’t resolved.

Paying a managing agent to generate endless correspondence rather than actually solve straightforward problems seems, in my opinion, completely asinine.

If you’re considering Neil Douglas, I’d seriously question what you’re actually paying them to manage.

Great outward journey, terrible return

I originally left a 5-star review after our transfer to Southend Airport for our flight to Morocco. The driver arrived early, was very kind and the journey was excellent. I even said I would return and leave another 5-star review if the return service was just as good.

Unfortunately, I’ve now returned — and the experience could not have been more different.

I called regularly before our flight home because I wanted to make sure the return booking hadn’t been forgotten. Despite that, they still managed to mess it up.

On the day, I was given misleading information about where the driver was, it seemed the driver had only been told about the job very late, and while I was trying to get a clear answer on the phone, the call was ended while we were still speaking. There was a lot of vague talking and excuses which felt like an attempt to buy time until the driver eventually arrived.

The first journey was clearly the exception. The return experience unfortunately matched many of the negative reviews I had seen.

I gave them every opportunity to get this right and even called ahead repeatedly to prevent exactly this situation.

Great driver on the outward journey, but the organisation and customer service on the return were unacceptable. For that reason, I’ve changed my review to 1 star.

⚠️ BE WARNED – VERY DISAPPOINTED WITH DR BIKES ⚠️

I would seriously consider ordering elsewhere and saving yourself the stress and inconvenience.

I ordered and paid for a 32amp ThunderBox on a Friday with next-day delivery. When it didn’t arrive, I had to chase the order myself. I was told they had been busy over the weekend, but as I pointed out, I had already placed and paid for my order on the Friday, so this should not have affected my order.

I was then told, “I’ll send it out today then.”

When the parcel eventually arrived 3 days later than expected, I opened it to discover they had sent me the cheaper 16amp ThunderBox instead of the 32amp version I had ordered and paid for.

Once again, I had to contact DR Bikes and explain the problem. Unfortunately, I was due to leave for a motorcycle tour of France within 12 hours and needed to get my equipment powered up, so I explained that I had little choice but to install the 16amp unit they had incorrectly supplied.

Their response was that if I fitted it, I could not return it.

While I was away, there were further emails backwards and forwards. In the end, I gave up and simply asked them to refund the next-day delivery charge and the price difference between the 32amp and 16amp units. I also said that if they felt some compensation was appropriate for all the inconvenience caused, I would appreciate it.

And guess what?

As of today, I still haven’t received the refund.

Mistakes happen, and I understand that. What disappoints me is how this has been handled from start to finish. I paid for next-day delivery, had to chase the order, received the wrong and cheaper product, and then had to continue chasing money that should have been refunded.

Very disappointing customer service from DR Bikes.

I will update this review if and when the matter is resolved.

one_star_reviews.text:
AVOID THIS PLACE. THEY ARE DISHONEST.

Camera City seem to spend more time replying to their bad Google reviews than communicating with their clients.

I took my Olympus MJU Zoom 105 into Camera City in November 2023. I paid £10 for a diagnosis - the sliding door mechanism was broken - so I paid £95 for a repair. When I collected the camera, I was told I needed to be very careful with it, so I didn't touch it until February for a special family trip. When I turned it on, it immediately broke. I emailed Camera City straight away with photos and a scan of the original receipt, explaining the situation.

When I came into the store, I spoke to Pany. He offered to help, despite the repair being outside the month warranty, and offered to keep the camera and replace the sliding door mechanism. I remember complimenting their customer service and flexibility to my dad at the time. Boy, I was SO wrong.

I received no communication or updates. I called regularly and visited in person every few months - a complete waste of time - and was told every time that the specific part hadn't shown up yet and that they'd contact me. I was never contacted.

I called and went in less frequently because life gets busy, and since I'd given them my number and email and they'd promised to be in touch, I trusted them to stick to their word.

Three years later, in 2026, still no news. I rang to say I thought it had gone on too long and I should just get my camera back. Pany replied, "Wow, it's been three years, I wouldn't even know where to find that camera." They clearly had lost it.

I went into the store the next day and Pany blamed me for the three years. He was extremely rude and gaslit me, insisting it was my fault for leaving it so long. When I showed him the scan of the receipt from 2023, and reminded him that I'd regularly rang them and visited and was told I would be contacted, he quickly changed tactics and said he couldn't remember me and that he needed the physical receipt.

I said either give me my camera back or an equivalent model. He offered to find me a different camera but said I'd still have to pay. I refused, and he said he needed time - when I asked how long, he said he'd contact me.... the same trap! I gave him a month.

I went in yesterday and he'd luckily found my camera - in terrible condition. I asked for my money back and he refused. He was rude and dishonest, still using the three years and the fact the camera is a really old model as a deflection. Right after a long distressing conversation, they said "we don't want you to be unhappy" and offered to fix my camera and said it wouldn't take long... which was HILARIOUS to me, because why didn't it get fixed three years ago?

He'll probably reply to this review blaming me and saying he needed physical receipts. It's all a deflection. It completely baffles me that a business would behave so dishonestly and unprofessionally.

I always want to support small independent businesses so it's a real shame. The lesson for me is, I should have checked the many, many other 1-star reviews and should have never trusted this place. I've wasted £105 and three years, all in good faith.

AVOID THIS PLACE. THEY ARE DISHONEST.

one_star_reviews.text:
I booked through Dial4Travel / Travel Junction, and my card was charged by Flights & Holidays UK Ltd. I paid £1,875.

I specifically requested a flight departing from Heathrow Terminal 2 because I was already at Terminal 2. After my payment was taken, I was told the flight was actually departing from Terminal 4, leaving insufficient time to get there and check in. The booking was cancelled within approximately 10–12 minutes.

Since then, I have repeatedly asked for the airline e-ticket number, airline booking reference/PNR and documentary proof that a ticket was actually issued. I have not been provided with these.

I have written communications from customer support on two separate occasions stating that the ticket was not issued. However, I was also given a conflicting explanation that the airline/supplier retained £500. Despite my repeated requests, I have not been provided with documentary evidence supporting that explanation.

I was subsequently informed by a manager that, after checking with the supplier, my outstanding £500 refund had been approved and would be processed within 5–7 working days. The refund was not received. There was then no resolution during the promised period, and approximately 11 days later I was instead told to await the outcome of my bank dispute.

For several months I have repeatedly contacted Dial4Travel, Travel Junction and Flights & Holidays UK Ltd by telephone and email. I have repeatedly requested the same basic information and supporting documents, but I have still not received the ticket evidence or a resolution.

I have also contacted the airline directly seeking confirmation concerning the reservation and ticket. I still have not received written confirmation of an e-ticket number, PNR or proof of ticket issuance.

I am particularly surprised by the owner’s public response stating that my booking could not be located. This matter has been the subject of extensive telephone calls and email correspondence with the company over several months. The company already holds my contact details, booking information, payment information and correspondence.

I will not publish my private booking reference, telephone number or email address on a public Google review simply to enable the company to identify a case it has already been corresponding about for months. If the company genuinely cannot locate the case, please review your own records or contact me privately using the information you already hold.

My request remains very simple:

If a ticket was issued, please provide the e-ticket number, PNR and documentary proof of issuance. If no ticket was issued, please explain why £500 of my money is still being retained.

one_star_reviews.text:
Have you been sent the wrong item by this company and then struggled to get it resolved? Read this.

I ordered a specific ProDec product and was sent a different Axus product instead. When I complained, I was told it was basically the same thing and initially got nowhere with a refund, partial refund or return.

I had to put everything in writing, quote my consumer rights and keep chasing before I eventually got my money back.

If you have had a similar problem, contact Citizens Advice Consumer Service as soon as possible. They can record what happened and pass relevant information to Trading Standards. Don't leave it too long, as other options such as a card chargeback can have their own time limits.

Keep your emails, photos and proof of exactly what you ordered and what you received. Don't just accept the first or any refusal.

I eventually got my refund, but getting a simple mistake corrected was far harder than it should have been.

Buy from somewhere else to be safe

one_star_reviews.text: Absolutely disgusting behaviour from course leaders. The head of the T level health and social cares attitude towards my daughter was absolutely disgraceful. My daughter suffers with both dyslexia and dyspraxia and upon year 11s gcse results day found out she has passed all of her subjects (with very respectable grades) apart from maths. We brought her into the college to look at alternative plans or if she is able to continue the course and re do maths alongside the main course. Upon arrival the course leader Wendy (as she introduced herself) proceeded to look my daughter up and down visibly (as she takes pride in her appearance for example blonde dyed hair and false nails) and we both began to explain my daughters situation. After hearing in a condescending tone she proceeded to ask my daughter “what happened to your maths then huh?” Speaking to her as if she was a failure because she failed GCSE maths which you can retake for free with the college. After me and my daughter proposed if she could take the course with re doing maths alongside she proceeded to respond with “have you not looked at hair and beauty instead? How about construction” when my daughter said she was not interested in either of those she proceeded to shout in my child’s face about needing to decide on the spot what she wanted to do and when she couldn’t think of an alternative route immediately she rolled her eyes again and shouted at her to try somewhere else because she would not have a place in this college. I understand they have no obligation to offer my daughter a place that is completely reasonable and valid although the attitude, disgust and overall prejudice she spoke to my daughter with was disgusting and I warn any parents wishing to send your kids to this college for health and social care against this. Luckily an abundance of other colleges have accepted her although this was still a negative experience on an already emotional day.

one_star_reviews.text:
I am very disappointed with the way I was treated at Wellington Hospital South Main Reception on 5 September 2026.

At approximately 6:50–6:55 a.m., I arrived at the hospital accompanying a patient during an emergency. We asked at the main reception whether there was somewhere we could charge the patient’s phone. The receptionist directed me to another man on the other side of the reception area, and I simply asked him where we could buy a charger.

To my surprise, the man became aggressive towards me and accused me of insulting him. I explained that I had not insulted him and even apologised in case there had been a misunderstanding. Despite this, he continued shouting at me, called me “silly,” and then started moving towards me in a way that I perceived as threatening, causing me to move back.

I found his behaviour intimidating, upsetting and frightening. I was particularly concerned because I was accompanying a patient during an emergency and did not expect to be treated this way by someone working at the hospital.

Patients and visitors should be treated with dignity and respect, especially when they are already dealing with the stress of an emergency.

I have submitted a formal complaint to the hospital and asked them to investigate the incident, identify the staff member involved, and review the CCTV footage from the main reception at the relevant time.

I hope the hospital takes this complaint seriously, establishes exactly what happened, and ensures that other patients and visitors do not have a similar experience.

Y Tarabe
